# Roadmap

## Goals

### C01 One clear owner for each relay step; no step lives in two tools

### C02 Keep the outer session's context small by moving deterministic work out of it

### C03 Use slicer and adjudicate only through their CLIs and JSON output

### C04 Follow slicer's relay contract by version, never by copying its text

### C10 One dashboard across projects: roadmaps, decisions and live relays with every agent, stage and progress

### C11 After v1: edit and reorder the roadmap from the dashboard, every edit a slicer CLI call

### C12 After v1: manage the decision queue from the dashboard, every change an adj CLI call made as the owner

### C13 Set up, launch and supervise parallel slice waves across vendors, owner-attended at checkpoints

### C14 User experience first: colorful, keyboard-driven TUI with mouse support

### C15 Small explicit state: ork owns only its registry, run records and UI preferences

### C18 Deterministic before model: tests, slicer check, fingerprint and report shape checked by ork before any model review

## Non-goals

### C05 No unattended runs; the owner attends every relay (open: adj scope.attended)

### C06 No tracking state of its own for items, slices, specs, readiness or decisions

### C07 No reading or writing .slicer/ or decisions/ files directly

### C08 No commits, pushes or merges unless the owner authorizes them for a run

### C09 Not an LLM; model work stays in the role agents

### C16 No scheduler: ork does not pick and run waves on its own

### C17 One workflow kind for now: the slice relay; no general pipeline language

Acceptance: (1) go test ./... passes with the same test count and no test removed or skipped; (2) go test ./internal/cli -count=1 wall time is at most 60 s and ./internal/engine at most 200 s, measured on the same machine and quoted before and after in the report; (3) no test depends on another's script file; (4) gofmt -l . and go vet ./... are clean. Source: .scratch/v11/ork-test-trim-proposal.md B1-B3. | done |
| 141 | [S285](slices/S285.md) | Separate round check command from the gate and landing check command | M | 2 |  | Owner 2026-11-04 chose: fix test speed first (S284, slicer s448), then run a faster check in implementer rounds and the full traced run at the gate and landing. Today one command serves every check (internal/engine/states.go:207 and :233, project key check_command, docs/state.md:49,78; ADR 0032 wants slicer's config key). For slicer the round command would add -p 'test*.py' to python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests (same tests, no line tracer, per .scratch/v11/test-trim-proposal.md); the full command keeps tests/test_affected.py's tracer and refreshes the affected-test map. Proposed (spec step must confirm with the owner and run adj check first; the key name, where it lives, and whether it is ork or slicer config are open): an optional round_check_command setting, used by implementer-round checks only; check_command stays for the gate and the landing re-check; unset means check_command everywhere. Acceptance: (1) with it unset, behavior and run logs are unchanged; (2) with it set, round checks run it and the log header names it, while the gate and landing run check_command; (3) the status and checks display name which command ran; (4) docs/state.md and docs/design.md document the key; (5) tests cover set, unset, and a failing round command followed by a passing gate. Order: after S284 and slicer s448 land and their measured savings are known; this is the second step (option 1 after option 3). | done |

| 154 | S299 | Vendor out marks: an owner's mark survives a daemon restart and can end at a set time (--until) | S | 1 |  | Waves 7-8, 2026-11-05 (friction F43): the owner's ork vendor out grok mark was lost three times, once by a daemon restart and twice silently when the daemon idled out (daemon_idle_minutes effective 10) while a wave start was held on a spec question waiting for the owner. The next run put Grok on the reviewer row and stopped (reviewer round 1 exited unclassified), costing a full implementer round (about 28 min) each time. Fact: an owner mark has no expiry (internal/daemon/vendors.go:30-31) but lives only in daemon memory; ork vendor list after the idle exit printed 'no vendor is out'. Needed: owner marks (ork vendor out) are written to ork's state directory and reloaded at daemon start, so they end only with ork vendor back; automatic rate-limit and credit marks keep their own expiry (S273). The help text 'a restart clears them' changes to match. Related: S273, S169, S182. Absorbed from S273 (retired into this row 2026-11-07): Owner 2026-11-03: the codex weekly limit message said it resets 7:12 AM on 4 Nov, but ork vendor out takes no end time, so the mark lasts until ork vendor back (or, today, a daemon restart). Still needed, as part of this row: (a) ork vendor out VENDOR --until TIME sets an owner mark that ends at TIME, is persisted with the other owner marks, and is shown with its end time in the footer and ork vendor list; (b) reading a reset time from the vendor's own message is done only once a real captured message with a reset time exists as a test fixture; until then automatic marks keep their fixed expiry (MarkOut sets Until to at plus VendorOutFor, internal/engine/vendors.go:162; owner marks have none, MarkOutOwner at internal/engine/vendors.go:172-182). Do not write a parser against a guessed message shape. · discovered from S280 | done |

Needed: a spec check whose round ended with denied read commands and no report is resumed once in the same session with the denials named and the allowed command forms from the brief's Done when section (S277); a second denial fails the check as today. One occurrence so far; S277's Done when may already prevent it. Related: S277, S266, S275. · Merged into S266 (same spec-check retry loop, speccheck.go:144-156): the denial case and what to re-check after S277 are in S266's findings. · discovered from S278 | retired |
